question.problem:
Suppose ${b}_{2}=p{b}_{1}+a$ and ${b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2}=0.$ If $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and ${b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$, find the value of $p.$ 

*Hint: You might wish to take the equation ${b}_{2}=p{b}_{1}+a$ and find the dot product of both sides with ${b}_{1}.$*
question.worked_solution:
First, we take the equation ${b}_{2}=p{b}_{1}+a$ and find the dot product of both sides with ${b}_{1}$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{2} & =p{b}_{1}+a \\ {b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2} & ={b}_{1}\cdot (p{b}_{1}+a) \\ {b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2} & ={b}_{1}\cdot (p{b}_{1})+({b}_{1}\cdot a) \\ {b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2} & =p({b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{1})+({b}_{1}\cdot a)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the formula for the dot product to compute the values of ${b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{1}\cdot a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{1} & ={b}_{1}^{2}+{b}_{2}^{2} \\  & ={2}^{2}+(-3)^{2} \\  & =4+9 \\  & =13 \\ {b}_{1}\cdot a & ={b}_{1}{a}_{1}+{b}_{2}{a}_{2} \\  & =2\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot (-1) \\  & =4+3 \\  & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting the values for ${b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{1},$ ${b}_{1}\cdot a,$ and ${b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{2} & =p({b}_{1}\cdot {b}_{1})+({b}_{1}\cdot a) \\ 0 & =p\cdot 13+7 \\ -13p & =7 \\ p & =-\frac{7}{13}.\end{aligned}
$$
